description: Comprehensive 25-MCQ test covering BISE past papers, repeating board questions, and subjective concepts for Chapter 15 (Homeostasis). Includes Osmoregulation, Excretion in Plants, Human Nephron, Liver Homeostatic Functions, Lithotripsy, and Thermoregulation.
title: Class 12 Biology: Chapter 15 — Homeostasis (Past Papers & Board Mastery)

questions.questionText: Protection of an internal environment from the harms of fluctuations in the external environment is termed as:
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the central mechanism that maintains dynamic internal stability (water, solutes, temperature) against external fluctuations (BISE Multan/Lahore/FSD).

questions.questionText: Lizards and other reptiles excrete their insoluble nitrogenous wastes primarily in the form of:
questions.explanation: Reptiles (including lizards), birds, and land snails are uricotelic and excrete uric acid paste requiring minimal water (~1 mL per gram of nitrogen) (BISE GRW).

questions.questionText: How much water is required for the excretion of one gram of ammonia nitrogen in ammonotelic animals?
questions.explanation: 1 gram of ammonia nitrogen requires approximately 500 ml of water to dilute and prevent cellular toxicity (BISE FSD/Multan).

questions.questionText: In terrestrial insects and arthropods, Malpighian tubules remove metabolic nitrogenous wastes directly from the:
questions.explanation: Insects have an open circulatory system; Malpighian tubules are suspended in hemolymph sinuses and absorb wastes into the hindgut (BISE Lahore/Sargodha).

questions.questionText: Calcium oxalate type of kidney stones accounts for approximately what percentage of all kidney stone incidences?
questions.explanation: Calcium oxalate stones account for 70% of kidney stones, while calcium phosphate accounts for 15% and uric acid for 10% (BISE FSD/RWP).

questions.questionText: Bats lack sweat glands; which of the following fluids do they use for evaporative heat dissipation in warm temperatures?
questions.explanation: Bats lack sweat glands and lick their body with saliva or use urine for evaporative cooling (BISE Lahore/Bahawalpur).

questions.questionText: Plants growing in salt marshes or saline soils close to the sea are physiologically adapted as:
questions.explanation: Halophytes live in high-salinity habitats and actively transport salts into vacuoles to lower their internal water potential (BISE Multan/FSD).

questions.questionText: Leaves that turn yellow in autumn and drop off to rid the plant of accumulated heavy metals and pigmented metabolic wastes are termed:
questions.explanation: Autumnal yellow leaves act as excretophores, sequestering metabolic wastes and toxic heavy metals out of the plant upon abscission (From Subjective LQ-01).

questions.questionText: In tomato plants, excess calcium and other cellular wastes are rendered harmless by being precipitated into crystal formations of:
questions.explanation: Plant vacuoles store organic and inorganic wastes, precipitating excess calcium into harmless calcium oxalate crystals (From Subjective LQ-01).

questions.questionText: The dark, dense central non-conducting wood in old trees where trees sequester chemical wastes and resins is called:
questions.explanation: In older stems, active xylem becomes heartwood (ebony) as it ceases water transport and accumulates metabolic wastes, oils, and tannins (From Subjective LQ-01).

questions.questionText: The phenomenon where plants (like conifers) actively secrete toxic chemical compounds from roots into the surrounding soil to inhibit competing plants is:
questions.explanation: Roots of certain plants actively secrete chemical compounds into the soil to inhibit the growth of nearby plant species via allelopathy (From Subjective LQ-01).

questions.questionText: In the human nephron, high hydrostatic pressure required for glomerular pressure filtration is generated because the:
options: Afferent arteriole is narrower than the efferent arteriole
Efferent arteriole is narrower than the afferent arteriole
Bowman's capsule has a thick impermeable membrane
Loop of Henle pumps sodium into the glomerulus
questions.explanation: The efferent arteriole is narrower than the afferent arteriole, creating high hydrostatic pressure (~55 mmHg) in the glomerulus that drives pressure filtration (From Subjective LQ-02).

questions.questionText: Which section of the human nephron is responsible for the selective reabsorption of approximately 80% of the glomerular filtrate, including all glucose and amino acids?
options: Descending limb of Loop of Henle
questions.explanation: The Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT) selectively reabsorbs ~80% of the filtrate, including 100% of essential nutrients (glucose, amino acids) and vitamins (From Subjective LQ-02).

questions.questionText: In the counter-current multiplier system of the human kidney, the thick ascending limb of the Loop of Henle is:
options: Permeable to water but impermeable to sodium ions
Impermeable to water and actively transports Na+ and Cl- into interstitial fluid
Permeable to both urea and water
The primary site of non-selective pressure filtration
questions.explanation: The ascending limb of Henle's loop is impermeable to water and actively pumps out Na+ and Cl- ions, creating hypertonic medullary interstitium (From Subjective LQ-02).

questions.questionText: In the hepatic urea cycle (ornithine cycle), which immediate intermediate is hydrolyzed by the enzyme arginase to release urea?
questions.explanation: Arginase cleaves arginine into urea and ornithine, which recycles to combine with ammonia and carbon dioxide (From Subjective LQ-03).

questions.questionText: The liver protects the body from toxic hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) produced during cellular metabolism by degrading it using which enzyme?
questions.explanation: Liver peroxisomes contain catalase, an enzyme that rapidly breaks down toxic hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen (From Subjective LQ-03).

questions.questionText: Animals whose internal osmolarity is isotonic to their surrounding marine environment and who do not actively adjust their osmotic state are known as:
questions.explanation: Osmoconformers (such as hagfishes and marine invertebrates) do not actively regulate internal osmolarity because body fluids are isotonic with seawater (From Subjective SQ-02).

questions.questionText: The physiological capability of desert animals like the kangaroo rat to tolerate severe dehydration without drinking free water by relying on metabolic water from dry seeds is called:
questions.explanation: Anhydrobiosis enables terrestrial animals (e.g. kangaroo rat) to survive without drinking liquid water by utilizing metabolic water from carbohydrate oxidation (From Subjective SQ-03).

questions.questionText: The non-invasive clinical technique that uses high-intensity acoustic shock waves (ESWL) to pulverize kidney stones into passable sand-like debris is:
questions.explanation: Extracorporeal Shock Wave Lithotripsy (ESWL) uses ultrasound/X-ray shock waves to shatter kidney stones into sand-sized particles (From Subjective SQ-04).

questions.questionText: Non-shivering thermogenesis in mammals generates body heat without muscular twitching through the action of thyroid hormones and adrenaline on:
questions.explanation: Non-shivering thermogenesis involves hormone-stimulated heat generation via mitochondrial uncoupling in brown fat (From Subjective SQ-05).

questions.questionText: Peptides and chemicals released by white blood cells and bacterial endotoxins that elevate the hypothalamic thermostat above 37°C causing fever (pyrexia) are:
questions.explanation: Pyrogens reset the hypothalamic thermostat to higher temperatures, inducing fever (pyrexia) to inhibit pathogen growth (From Subjective SQ-06).

questions.questionText: Antidiuretic Hormone (ADH / Vasopressin) increases the permeability of which nephron segments to promote water reabsorption?
options: Collecting Ducts and Distal Convoluted Tubules
Ascending limb of Loop of Henle
questions.explanation: ADH acts on late DCT and collecting duct cells, promoting aquaporin insertion and water reabsorption back into the blood (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: Freshwater bony fishes constantly take in water osmotically; how do they maintain osmotic equilibrium?
options: Drinking continuous amounts of water and producing concentrated urine
Excreting large volumes of very dilute (hypotonic) urine and absorbing salts actively via gills
Accumulating large amounts of urea in their blood
questions.explanation: Freshwater bony fishes overcome water gain by producing copious dilute urine and active uptake of salts through specialized gill ionocytes (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: The loss of liquid water droplets through special pores called hydathodes along the tips and margins of leaves in high humidity conditions is termed:
questions.explanation: Guttation is the exudation of xylem liquid water droplets via hydathodes caused by root pressure during nighttime or high humidity (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: Which hormone released by the adrenal cortex acts on distal renal tubules to increase sodium (Na+) reabsorption and potassium (K+) excretion?
questions.explanation: Aldosterone stimulates sodium reabsorption in exchange for potassium secretion in the distal tubule and collecting duct, maintaining fluid balance (Important Board Past Paper Question).

title: Class 12 Biology: Chapter 21 — Cell Cycle (Past Papers & Board Mastery)
subject: Biology

questions.questionText: Condensation of chromosomes during Prophase I of Meiosis reaches its maximum level in which sub-stage?
questions.explanation: During Diakinesis, chromosomes reach maximum condensation, chiasmata terminalize to chromosome tips, and nucleoli disappear (BISE GRW/Sahiwal).

questions.questionText: Down's syndrome (Mongolism) is caused by chromosomal non-disjunction leading to trisomy of which human autosome?
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome is an autosomal trisomy (2n+1 = 47) caused by non-disjunction of chromosome pair 21 (BISE Lahore/FSD).

questions.questionText: During the Leptotene sub-stage of Prophase I, chromosomes appear as thin visible threads displaying bead-like local swellings known as:
questions.explanation: Chromomeres are bead-like coiled chromatin condensations visible along chromosomes in Leptotene (From Subjective LQ-14).

questions.questionText: The highly specific, point-for-point pairing of homologous maternal and paternal chromosomes (synapsis) occurs during which stage of Prophase I?
questions.explanation: Zygotene is characterized by synapsis, where homologous chromosomes pair lengthwise to form bivalents (tetrads) (From Subjective LQ-14).

questions.questionText: Crossing over, the physical exchange of non-sister chromatid genetic segments between homologous chromosomes, takes place during:
questions.explanation: In Pachytene, non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes exchange segments at chiasmata, producing genetic recombination (From Subjective LQ-14).

questions.questionText: Homologous chromosomes begin to repel and separate from each other, remaining connected only at points of crossing over (chiasmata), during:
questions.explanation: Diplotene begins when synaptic forces dissolve and paired homologous chromosomes repel each other except at chiasmata (From Subjective LQ-14).

questions.questionText: In the Diakinesis stage of meiotic Prophase I, the shifting and sliding of chiasmata from centromeric regions toward the chromosome ends is called:
questions.explanation: Terminalization is the displacement of chiasmata from the centromere towards the ends of chromosomes during Diakinesis (From Subjective LQ-14).

questions.questionText: The failure of homologous chromosomes to separate during Meiosis I or sister chromatids during Meiosis II is called:
questions.explanation: Non-disjunction is the failure of chromosome separation at anaphase, resulting in gametes with 2n+1 or 2n-1 chromosome numbers (From Subjective LQ-15).

questions.questionText: A human male exhibiting tall stature, enlarged breast tissue (gynecomastia), small testes, and azoospermia with a 47, XXY karyotype has:
questions.explanation: Klinefelter's syndrome (47, XXY) affects phenotypic males with testicular atrophy, sterility, and gynecomastia (From Subjective LQ-15 & SQ-29).

questions.questionText: A phenotypic female with a 45, XO karyotype presenting with short stature, webbed neck, missing ovaries, and primary amenorrhea suffers from:
questions.explanation: Turner's syndrome (45, XO) is a sex chromosome monosomy resulting in phenotypic females with streak ovaries and webbed neck (From Subjective LQ-15 & SQ-29).

questions.questionText: The risk of non-disjunction causing Down's syndrome increases markedly with advancing maternal age, reaching approximately 1 in 40 births when the mother is:
questions.explanation: Maternal age over 40 dramatically elevates non-disjunction risk to 1 in 40 births due to aged primary oocytes arrested since birth (From Subjective LQ-15).

questions.questionText: Genetically programmed cellular suicide wherein a dying cell shrinks, condenses its chromatin, and is phagocytosed without provoking tissue inflammation is:
questions.explanation: Apoptosis is programmed cell death: the cell shrinks, forms apoptotic blebs, and is phagocytosed cleanly without inflammation (From Subjective SQ-27).

questions.questionText: Accidental cell death resulting from acute injury, severe infection, or hypoxia characterized by cellular swelling, membrane rupture, and intense local inflammation is:
questions.explanation: Necrosis is accidental cell death caused by trauma/toxins; cells swell, lyse, and release enzymes causing severe inflammatory response (From Subjective SQ-27).

questions.questionText: During human embryological limb morphogenesis, the sculpting and separation of individual digits (fingers and toes) is mediated by:
options: Rapid mitotic division of epidermal cells
Programmed cell death (Apoptosis) of interdigital webbing
Necrotic breakdown due to oxygen deprivation
questions.explanation: Apoptosis removes the interdigital tissue webs during human embryo hand and foot development (From Subjective SQ-27).

questions.questionText: The complete mitotic apparatus in an animal cell consists of two radiating asters around centrosomes and the:
questions.explanation: The mitotic apparatus comprises two asters and the mitotic spindle fibers (kinetochore and polar microtubules) (From Subjective SQ-28).

questions.questionText: The specialized spindle microtubules that attach directly to the protein disk situated at the centromere of each condensed chromosome are:
questions.explanation: Kinetochore microtubules attach to the kinetochore protein complex on centromeres to align and separate sister chromatids (From Subjective SQ-28).

questions.questionText: In which sub-phase of the eukaryotic cell cycle interphase does DNA replication and histone synthesis take place?
questions.explanation: During the S (Synthesis) phase of interphase, nuclear DNA is completely replicated and chromosome duplication occurs (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: Mature human nerve cells and skeletal muscle fibers that cease cell division and remain metabolically functional exit the cell cycle into:
questions.explanation: Cells that permanently or semi-permanently stop dividing enter the G0 (quiescent / non-dividing) phase (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: During the G2 phase of interphase, the cell primarily synthesizes energy reserves and specialized structural proteins required for:
questions.explanation: The G2 phase prepares the cell for mitosis by synthesizing tubulin proteins, spindle elements, and accumulating ATP (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: The crucial restriction checkpoint in the eukaryotic cell cycle that commits the cell to either proceed irreversibly to DNA replication or withdraw to G0 is:
questions.explanation: The G1/S checkpoint (restriction point) determines whether the cell has sufficient resources and intact DNA before committing to replication (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: In dividing plant cells, cytokinesis occurs through the assembly of Golgi-derived pectin vesicles across the equatorial plane to form a:
questions.explanation: In plant cells, cytokinesis is mediated by the phragmoplast, which fuses Golgi-derived vesicles into the new cell plate (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: During which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids synchronously separate at their centromeres and migrate toward opposite spindle poles?
questions.explanation: Anaphase begins when centromeres divide and sister chromatids are pulled apart as individual daughter chromosomes to opposite poles (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: At which mitotic stage do all duplicated chromosomes become maximally condensed and aligned along the equatorial plane of the spindle?
questions.explanation: During Metaphase, kinetochore fibers orient all chromosomes at the equatorial/metaphase plate midway between the two poles (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: The master molecular engine driving the cell through different checkpoints of the cell cycle is composed of heterodimeric complexes of:
questions.explanation: Cell cycle transitions are regulated by Cyclin proteins binding to and activating Cyclin-Dependent Kinases (Cdks) (Important Board Past Paper Question).

questions.questionText: Uncontrolled, uninhibited mitotic cell division caused by mutations in proto-oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes that invade neighboring tissues is termed:
questions.explanation: Cancer/malignancy is characterized by breakdown of cell cycle controls, loss of contact inhibition, and autonomous proliferation (Important Board Past Paper Question).

description: Comprehensive 25-MCQ test covering BISE past papers, repeating board questions, and subjective concepts for Chapter 21 (Cell Cycle). Includes Interphase (G1, S, G2, G0), Mitosis phases, Meiosis I Prophase sub-stages, Non-disjunction syndromes, Mitotic apparatus, and Apoptosis vs Necrosis.
